text:
sam_infra: Heads-up — ACME onboarding asks for a Dedicated pool in eu-west with 24/7 committed throughput but wants to mix in spot instances for cost. How do we size the commit so they don't hit throttles during peak windows AND we don't overcommit/lose margin when spot preempts?
zoe_prod: What's their 95th percentile token/sec target? also: region has limited A100 spot supply atm. :thinking:
liam_cost: Last convo said target ~4800 tokens/s sustained, spikes up to ~9k tokens/s for 10m bursts. They want 80% cost savings target on average via spot blend.
maria_sales: They signed for a throughput SLA for critical flows (checkout, auth) — those need private capacity fallback. We can't degrade those.
nana_sre: we should treat committed capacity as the safety net for SLA traffic, route non-critical to spot + best-effort. Need clear routing policy and fallback latencies documented.
sam_infra: agreed. Quick sizing sketch: 
```
# rough calculation
customer_target_rps = 120
avg_tokens_per_call = 40
tokens_per_sec = customer_target_rps * avg_tokens_per_call  # 4800
gpu_tokens_per_sec = 800  # per GPU baseline for chosen model+quant
gpus_needed = ceil(tokens_per_sec / gpu_tokens_per_sec)  # 6
commit_floor = ceil(gpus_needed * 0.8)  # 5 => keep headroom for safety
```
sam_infra: so commit 5 GPUs reserved, allow autoscale to add 1-2 on burst (paid as burst/reserved mapping), and allow 2 spot GPUs for cost blending. That gives nominal 7 GPUs but only 5 are guaranteed.
liam_cost: billing caveat — cloud invoices charge preempted spot hours as partials sometimes, and our internal billing used to double-count preempted allocation if not reconciled. Need to confirm we only bill customer for successful token-served time on spot vs commit. I'll open billing ticket.
maria_sales: customer will accept a commit floor + burst pricing if we make the buy clear in contract. They asked for a forecast table showing monthly $ delta for 0/10/20/30% spot mix.
nana_sre: operational checklist: 
- implement policy: route critical routes -> reserved pool; non-critical -> spot pool
- on spot preempt event: failover path -> reserved, with <300ms queueing target
- telemetry: emit per-route token/sec, per-GPU utilization, preempt_count per zone
- alert: preempt_rate > 2/hour for >5m -> paging + holdback scaling

zoe_prod: can we simulate preemptions in eu-west stage to measure failover latency? I can run a chaos job that kills spot nodes every X min and measure tail latency.
sam_infra: yes please. Also need to run a cost-sensitivity calc for billing team: what's the marginal cost if spot returns partial-hour billing vs full-hour? Put numbers for cloud provider (e.g., spot billed in 1m increments but preemption kills work -> we may re-run on reserved).
liam_cost: I'll pull last quarter invoices for eu-west and run preempt reconciliation. Also check our internal meter: do we tag preempted VM UUIDs and reconcile token counts? Past bug: preempted containers kept emitting CPU metrics but no tokens, leading to skew.
nana_sre: action items: @liam_cost open billing investigation ticket; @zoe_prod run chaos preempt sim in stage; @sam_infra draft commit+burst proposal and a 4-row forecast table for sales; I'll add runbook snippets for failover.
maria_sales: ping me once forecast is ready, I'll align contract language. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy queue: scheduled chaos job (zone-a spot-kill) -> 2187654405 (ETA)
sam_infra: thanks all — aim to have a proposal doc + numbers by EOW. If experiments show >10% tail penalty on 95th latency when spot preempts, we should move to a 90/10 commit/spot split instead.
liam_cost: noted. I'll include sensitivity to preemption frequency in the delta table.
nana_sre: also note network egress pricing across AZs in eu-west — cross-AZ fallbacks can add $$; avoid cross-region fallback for committed SLA traffic.
zoe_prod: I'll also surface the model variant quantization impact — quantized models increase tokens/sec per GPU (so fewer GPUs needed). Good knob for cost.
sam_infra: perfect. closing thread for now, will post the draft PR with numbers.
